from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 6  # sources
    J = 10  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [245, 208, 220, 240, 183, 208]
    demands = [18, 49, 14, 35, 60, 12, 17, 39, 42, 29]
    cost_matrix = [[16.15, 13.12, 12.3, 8.11, 27.77, 27.68, 22.41, 24.09, 12.11, 6.12], [23.28, 5.44, 4.64, 15.26, 22.55, 25.48, 14.93, 12.62, 13.19, 25.0], [18.5, 29.15, 24.96, 3.22, 15.45, 7.3, 12.42, 13.74, 20.65, 23.56], [27.77, 28.37, 17.09, 28.28, 13.82, 24.82, 7.66, 11.39, 9.08, 15.72], [12.6, 11.59, 18.25, 5.7, 9.03, 9.8, 25.42, 23.14, 7.27, 10.91], [21.27, 27.16, 11.8, 4.04, 3.13, 27.4, 23.74, 29.74, 18.87, 13.87]]
    emission_matrix = [[9.37, 2.93, 10.68, 13.78, 9.79, 5.86, 14.97, 2.19, 16.91, 5.55], [15.61, 4.67, 9.0, 6.81, 7.09, 7.39, 11.91, 15.75, 16.92, 9.11], [16.89, 4.29, 11.03, 20.0, 7.16, 17.85, 10.73, 6.41, 1.34, 14.54], [5.71, 15.32, 14.59, 9.9, 13.58, 2.71, 4.32, 10.91, 11.94, 10.22], [16.78, 15.55, 7.65, 8.77, 8.88, 15.39, 2.7, 5.21, 14.58, 16.31], [16.06, 13.18, 14.53, 19.79, 10.12, 1.0, 5.26, 12.79, 2.24, 6.62]]
    fixed_costs = [[294, 118, 200, 174, 154, 171, 292, 255, 240, 70], [205, 192, 66, 165, 218, 207, 80, 234, 263, 234], [241, 168, 104, 262, 273, 70, 77, 188, 243, 247], [201, 246, 142, 288, 192, 182, 294, 168, 204, 88], [268, 80, 225, 225, 220, 241, 220, 292, 219, 101], [93, 56, 129, 164, 251, 110, 262, 157, 183, 174]]
    moq = [[18, 7, 7, 7, 17, 13, 18, 19, 17, 11], [19, 5, 7, 5, 10, 10, 7, 14, 11, 16], [10, 5, 14, 14, 20, 6, 5, 5, 11, 15], [14, 8, 15, 8, 11, 17, 6, 14, 7, 7], [12, 16, 18, 10, 5, 13, 6, 16, 12, 13], [19, 5, 18, 6, 19, 18, 6, 13, 10, 14]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Supply Chain and Finance Leadership
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing transportation cost and carbon across our warehouse-to-store network
Date: Current planning cycle

Context
Our warehouse-to-store network faces a clear trade-off: the lowest-dollar lanes often carry higher carbon intensity, while cleaner lanes can be more expensive. As we scale replenishment and navigate tightening sustainability commitments and cost targets, we need a single, pragmatic plan that reflects management’s priorities on cost versus emissions, without compromising service or operational feasibility.

Operational rules that shape the plan
- Route activation has an upfront setup fee. Turning on any warehouse-to-store lane triggers a fixed charge tied to carrier contracting, paperwork, and dock readiness. This fee applies once per planning cycle for each active lane and is independent of shipped volume.
- Active lanes must move at least a minimum order. To avoid inefficiencies and reject partial loads, any lane we activate must carry at least the predefined minimum quantity. If a lane is not activated, it carries no volume and incurs no activation fee.
- Each store limits the number of supplying warehouses. To keep receiving, vendor management, and slotting practical, each store will accept deliveries from only a capped number of different warehouses within the period.

Planning boundaries
- Warehouse supplies are finite; outbound allocations cannot exceed available inventory and labor capacity.
- Store demands are firm minimums; each location must receive at least its required volume within the period.
- All shipments must respect the activation rule and minimum order policy above.
- Each store’s inbound plan must respect the supplier cap noted above.

Management priority
Leadership has established relative importance weights for cost and for emissions. These weights govern how we trade off cheaper but more carbon-intensive lanes against cleaner but pricier options. We will apply these weights to the variable portions of spend and carbon, while treating route activation fees as a separate fixed component.

What we will optimize for
We will identify which lanes to activate and how much to move on each active lane to:
- Satisfy every store’s minimum volume while staying within each warehouse’s available supply.
- Respect the minimum order on any activated lane and avoid activating lanes that we do not use.
- Keep each store’s supply base within the allowed cap.
- Achieve the lowest blended total that reflects leadership’s priorities by:
  - Applying the cost weight to all per-unit shipping charges across activated lanes.
  - Applying the emission weight to all per-unit carbon across activated lanes.
  - Adding the full activation fees for any lanes we choose to turn on (these fixed fees are not weighted).

Why this matters
This approach turns abstract trade-offs into a clear, implementable routing plan that keeps us within budget guardrails, advances our climate commitments, and avoids operational churn at docks and on the road. It also provides transparency: if leadership adjusts the relative importance of cost and emissions, we can quickly test alternatives and quantify the impact on total spend, footprint, and lane activation.

Next steps
- Confirm current warehouse supplies, store demands, per-lane variable costs, and per-lane carbon rates; validate route activation fees and lane-level minimum order quantities.
- Validate the current cap on the number of warehouses allowed per store.
- Run scenarios with the agreed weights and review the recommended active lanes, volumes, expected spend, and expected carbon footprint.
- Align on exceptions for strategic lanes (e.g., disaster recovery, new store ramp-up) if needed.
- Finalize and communicate the plan to carriers, DC operations, and store operations.
